rounds.name: How You Think and Approach Change

mappingNotation: Each mapping has category, construct, role (primary=1.0; secondary=0.5), and a per-map conceptual rationale. Personality mappings occur only on personality items.
mappingWeightResolution: For every entry in an item's maps array, its exact numeric weight is weightsByRole[entry[2]]: primary is 1.0 and secondary is 0.5. Items marked contextualFor are deliberately unscored and have no map/weight.

coreQuestions.text: When a group has an unmet need, I help start a practical response even when no clear path exists.
maps: Starting a new shared response is direct evidence of the Apostle orientation.
The behavior is pioneering a new work.
Starting a shared response can require initial direction, but does not establish leadership alone.
Taking the first practical step is observable initiative.

coreQuestions.text: I turn a new idea into clear steps that other people can take.
maps: Building a path others can join is a starting-and-building behavior.
It directly reflects establishing a new work.
Breaking work into clear steps is organizing.
It connects an idea with coordinated action.

coreQuestions.text: I look for respectful ways to build relationships in a community that is new to me.
maps: The behavior directly concerns respectful work across communities.
It requires building trust with people.
It requires adjusting to an unfamiliar context.

coreQuestions.text: I organize people, information, or supplies so a group can carry out a plan.
maps: The item directly measures arranging work.

coreQuestions.text: When a team is waiting to begin, I am willing to suggest a first next step.
maps: Moving an unstarted team into action is an initiating orientation.
Suggesting direction for a waiting team is leadership behavior.

coreQuestions.text: When several good options are possible, I identify the one most likely to help a group reach its longer goal.
maps: The item directly assesses long-term priority thinking.
Selecting a workable option addresses a practical decision problem.

coreQuestions.text: I notice when a group’s actions do not match the values it says are important.
maps: Noticing value-action inconsistency is an observable health-and-truth orientation.
The behavior is careful distinction between stated and observed patterns.

coreQuestions.text: When I see a concern that could harm people, I can name it respectfully.
maps: Respectfully naming a harmful concern is a truth-telling behavior.
Naming a concern clearly uses communication.
Speaking up about possible harm supports protection and fairness.

coreQuestions.text: Before offering advice in a difficult situation, I listen for important details and weigh them carefully.
maps: The item describes thoughtful, situation-sensitive counsel.
It explicitly requires listening before responding.
It explicitly requires weighing meaningful details.

coreQuestions.text: I pay attention when someone may be left out or treated without dignity.
maps: The item directly reflects awareness of another person’s wellbeing.
It directly concerns exclusion and dignity.

coreQuestions.text: I notice a small concern early and raise it before it becomes harder to address.
maps: Early attention to a developing concern is a distinct health-oriented behavior.
It directly measures recognizing a concern needing attention.

coreQuestions.text: When I have a spiritual impression, I pause and seek wise confirmation before acting on it.
maps: The general behavior of testing an impression supports reflective discernment.

coreQuestions.text: I can distinguish between a strong personal feeling and a conclusion supported by what I have learned.
maps: It directly measures separating feeling from supported conclusion.

coreQuestions.text: When people disagree about a spiritual concern, I encourage patient listening and shared discernment.
I build genuine relationships with people who are curious about Christian faith.
maps: Relationship-building with faith explorers is direct Evangelist evidence.
It supports helping people engage Christian faith.
The observable behavior is building trust.

coreQuestions.text: I can explain why Christian faith matters in words that connect with another person’s questions.
maps: Explaining faith in connection with a person’s questions is an Evangelist behavior.
It directly supports communicating the gospel.
It observes adapting words to an audience.

coreQuestions.text: I make room for honest questions when someone is exploring faith.
maps: Creating space for faith exploration is direct Evangelist evidence.
The behavior supports a person responding to faith.
Making room for questions requires receptive listening.

coreQuestions.text: I learn from local people before offering help in a culture or community different from my own.
maps: The behavior directly reflects humble cross-cultural ministry.
It requires changing one’s approach for the context.

coreQuestions.text: I help a newcomer understand how to take part without expecting them to already know our ways.
maps: It indicates culturally humble inclusion across unfamiliar practices.
It directly creates a received and accessible environment.
It helps another person feel seen and included.
It directly observes making participation welcoming.
Adjusting expectations for unfamiliar practices is a limited, context-specific adaptability signal.

coreQuestions.text: I notice progress in people and tell them what I see with honest encouragement.
maps: The behavior is specific, timely encouragement.
It directly observes recognizing and strengthening potential.

coreQuestions.text: I follow up with people after a difficult time instead of assuming someone else will do it.
maps: Steady follow-up after difficulty is direct care-over-time evidence.
The behavior is ongoing relational care.
Follow-up after difficulty can express mercy.

coreQuestions.text: I help people recognize one practical next step in their growth.
maps: Guiding a person’s next growth step is Shepherd evidence.
The item directly supports development of another person.

coreQuestions.text: I can stay present with someone through a long or complicated season.
maps: Sustained care through changing seasons is a Shepherd behavior.
It reflects patient spiritual and relational care.
Compassion amid ongoing complexity is direct mercy evidence.
The item directly measures sustained compassionate presence.

coreQuestions.text: When someone needs help, I look for a practical way to support them while protecting their dignity.
maps: The item directly observes care for wellbeing.

coreQuestions.text: I keep praying for a person or need over time, even when I do not yet see an answer.
maps: The behavior is persistent focused prayer.

coreQuestions.text: I offer a hopeful word or prayer when someone feels discouraged.
maps: A hopeful word to a discouraged person is direct encouragement evidence.

coreQuestions.text: When an outcome is uncertain, I continue to pray and take the next faithful action I can see.
maps: Trustful action amid uncertainty directly supports this gift’s stated construct.

coreQuestions.text: I enjoy learning a truth from Scripture or faith well enough to explain it in clear, simple language.
maps: Making a faith-related idea clear is direct Teacher orientation evidence.
The behavior is clear explanation of biblical or faith truth.

coreQuestions.text: I study a Scripture or faith topic carefully and organize what I learn so another person can use it.
maps: Study and usable organization support a Teacher orientation.
It reflects understanding and communicating spiritual insight.
Organized learning can support teaching but does not necessarily include teaching.
Preparing learning for another person supports explanation.
Arranging learned material is a limited organizing signal.

coreQuestions.text: I use an example, story, or picture to help another person understand a message from Scripture or faith.
maps: Adjusting a faith-related explanation through examples supports understanding.
The behavior directly supports teaching biblical or faith truth.
It directly measures a clear explanatory method.
The behavior is using memorable communication forms.

coreQuestions.text: I ask questions to learn where someone is confused before I explain a Scripture idea more.
maps: Responding to a learner’s understanding is a Teacher behavior.
It supports helping another understand biblical or faith truth.
It seeks the learner’s next need.

coreQuestions.text: I share an insight from Scripture or faith in a way that helps another person think it through.
maps: Sharing faith insight for understanding can support teaching, but is not enough by itself.
It directly reflects communicating spiritual insight.
Helping another think an insight through supports explanation.
It requires expressing an idea accessibly.

coreQuestions.text: I offer perspective that considers both the facts of a situation and the people affected.
maps: It weighs relevant dimensions of a situation.

coreQuestions.text: I use a practical, visual, or musical skill to help a group take part in a shared activity.
maps: The item directly concerns practical or artistic skill used to serve others.
It explicitly uses practical skill for a shared activity.
Visual or musical skill is a limited creative signal.

coreQuestions.text: I use music to help a group participate in worship or shared reflection.
maps: The behavior directly fits musical service that encourages worship.
Practiced musical contribution is a particular artistic craft.
Music is a direct creative-expression behavior.

coreQuestions.text: I prepare and practice an artistic or technical contribution so it serves a group well.
maps: Careful preparation of artistic or technical work is craftsmanship.
Technical preparation can use hands-on skill.

coreQuestions.text: As an unmarried person, I experience my singleness as a healthy part of my devotion, relationships, and service.
coreQuestions.eligibility: show only when participant identifies as unmarried; otherwise resolve as N/A
maps: This is a direct self-reflection on the source taxonomy’s celibacy construct.

coreQuestions.text: As an unmarried person, I seek wise support as I discern how to live and serve faithfully in this season.
coreQuestions.eligibility: show only when participant identifies as unmarried; otherwise resolve as N/A
maps: It is a distinct discernment-and-support indicator within the existing celibacy construct.

coreQuestions.text: As an unmarried person, I have freedom to focus my present season on healthy relationships and service.
coreQuestions.eligibility: show only when participant identifies as unmarried; otherwise resolve as N/A
maps: It is a distinct reflection on freedom for present service; it must not be treated as a value judgment.

coreQuestions.text: I willingly choose to use less of my own resources so I can share more with people or a need.
maps: The behavior directly reflects choosing less in order to serve.
Sharing resources is related, though voluntary simplicity is a distinct construct.

coreQuestions.text: I consider whether a simpler choice could free resources for generosity or service.
maps: It is a distinct reflective indicator of voluntary simplicity for service.

coreQuestions.text: I can live with less when that choice helps me serve others with greater freedom.
maps: It is direct evidence of willing simplicity for service.

coreQuestions.text: I share money, time, or useful resources thoughtfully when I see a real need.
maps: The item directly reflects generous sharing of resources.

coreQuestions.text: After a busy week, I usually recover energy more through quiet time or through being with people.
maps: Neutral recovery preference; no ministry behavior is used.

coreQuestions.text: In a new group, I tend to think privately first or talk through what I notice.
maps: Neutral processing preference; no ministry behavior is used.

coreQuestions.text: When thinking through an idea, I prefer to reflect alone or exchange thoughts with someone.
maps: Neutral thought-processing preference; no ministry behavior is used.

coreQuestions.text: When choosing between good options, I first consider the people affected or the most consistent principle.
maps: Neutral decision preference; it does not infer compassion or justice strength.

coreQuestions.text: A decision feels strongest to me when it protects relationships or when it follows a clear standard.
maps: Neutral preference for a decision lens.

coreQuestions.text: When people are affected differently by a choice, I first weigh personal impact or fairness and consistency.
maps: Neutral trade-off preference, not a measure of mercy or advocacy.

coreQuestions.text: When beginning a project, I prefer to keep options open or settle the plan early.
If circumstances change, I prefer to adjust as I go or return to a clear plan.
maps: Neutral response-to-change preference; it does not score adaptability strength.

coreQuestions.text: I feel most comfortable when next steps can stay flexible or are already decided.
When I first look at a situation, I notice immediate details or broader patterns.
maps: Neutral attention preference, not a measure of discernment or strategy.

coreQuestions.text: I naturally ask what needs attention now or what this could become.
I prefer to clarify practical steps or connect ideas and possibilities.
maps: Neutral contribution preference; it does not score organization or strategy.

coreQuestions.text: When work needs to begin, I prefer to strengthen an existing effort or create the first movement.
maps: Neutral action preference, not a leadership or apostleship inference.

coreQuestions.text: I feel most useful when I improve what is already working or turn a new idea into action.
maps: Neutral preference; no strength or ministry mapping.

coreQuestions.text: In a group task, I prefer to take a supporting role or start a new direction.
My ideal weekly rhythm has steady repetition or frequent variety and change.
When several needs appear at once, I prefer a sustainable pace or a fast-moving response.
maps: Neutral pace preference; it does not infer resilience or initiative.

coreQuestions.text: I sustain my best work through predictable rhythms or a changing mix of responsibilities.
When developing an idea, I prefer focused time alone or brainstorming with other people.
maps: Neutral work-style preference, not a relational-strength inference.

coreQuestions.text: I do my best work with personal ownership or with shared responsibility and feedback.
Responsibility feels healthiest when I can own a task or when I can work through it with others.

optionalSpecialExperienceModule.text: I have experienced prayer connected with healing in a way I believe may have helped another person.
maps: Experience-specific healing reflection; it makes no APEST or personality inference.

optionalSpecialExperienceModule.text: I seek appropriate care and wise guidance when praying with someone about healing.
When I pray for healing, I remain humble about the outcome and respectful of the person.
I have experienced an interpretation of tongues that I believe was helpful to a gathered community.
maps: Experience-specific interpretation reflection; no APEST or personality inference.

optionalSpecialExperienceModule.text: When considering an interpretation of tongues, I welcome confirmation and pastoral guidance.
I approach interpretation of tongues with humility and care for the gathered community.
I have experienced an extraordinary answer to prayer in a situation involving me.
maps: Experience-specific reflection; it does not claim verification of a miracle.

optionalSpecialExperienceModule.text: I seek wise confirmation before describing an experience as an extraordinary work of God.
I can pray expectantly while remaining humble about what will happen.
I have shared an impression I believed God was prompting for another person’s encouragement or direction.
maps: Tradition-sensitive, experience-specific prophecy reflection; distinct from Prophet APEST.

optionalSpecialExperienceModule.text: Before sharing a spiritual impression, I seek discernment and appropriate confirmation.
I hold spiritual impressions humbly and remain open to correction.
I have experienced speaking in tongues or a spiritual utterance that I believe was given by the Holy Spirit.
maps: Experience-specific tongues reflection; no personality or APEST inference.

optionalSpecialExperienceModule.text: I welcome pastoral guidance and confirmation as I understand experiences of tongues.
I practice tongues with care for the gathered community and its shared discernment.
